data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'l-y-n', meaning 'to send' or 'to call'. Layyina can be translated as 'she who sends' or 'she who calls'. In Islamic tradition, it can symbolize the role of a spiritual guide or messenger. The name Layyina carries the meaning “Ambassador, Messenger” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Layyina usually hope their child will grow to embody ambassador, messenger and live with faith, good character and purpose.
